docuLanguageListResources.title: Commission unconditionally approves Deutsche Börse's acquisition of Allfunds
docuLanguageListResources.leadText: The European Commission has unconditionally approved, under the EU Merger Regulation, the proposed acquisition by Deutsche Börse of Allfunds.

docuLanguageListResources.leadText: Statement Special EUCO

docuLanguageListResources.title: Temu commits to complying with EU consumer protection rules following action by national authorities
docuLanguageListResources.leadText: Following a coordinated action by the European Commission and the Consumer Protection Cooperation (CPC) Network, the online marketplace Temu has committed to bring several of its commercial practices in line with EU consumer protection laws. The CPC Network accepted Temu's commitments today.

Commission issues positive opinion on the compatibility of a sustainability agreement in the French wine sector with competition rules for agriculture
docuLanguageListResources.leadText: The Commission issued today its second opinion regarding the compatibility of a sustainability agreement with competition rules for the agricultural sector.

docuLanguageListResources.title: Commission fines Firmenich, Givaudan and IFF €471.9 million for participating in an international fragrance cartel
docuLanguageListResources.leadText: The Commission has fined Firmenich, Givaudan and International Flavors & Fragrances (IFF), the three largest worldwide fragrance producers, a total of €471.9 million for participating in an international cartel in the fragrance sector, in breach of EU competition rules.

docuLanguageListResources.title: Commission prolongs State aid framework to support sectors affected by Middle East crisis until June 2027
docuLanguageListResources.leadText: The European Commission has prolonged the Middle East Crisis Temporary State aid Framework (METSAF) by six months until 30 June 2027.

docuLanguageListResources.title: Speech by President von der Leyen at the European Parliament plenary debate on Europe's role and capacity to protect the international order and secure a just and lasting peace for Ukraine
Commission proposes Quantum Act and new Sovereign Tech Equity Fund to strengthen Europe's industrial capacity and security
docuLanguageListResources.leadText: The European Commission today proposed the Quantum Act, a new framework to help turn Europe's quantum research into products and services, strengthen supply chains and prepare Europe's digital systems for post-quantum cryptography. The proposal also lays the groundwork for the Sovereign Tech Equity Fund (STEF).

docuLanguageListResources.title: Joint statement by the Commission and the High Representative ahead of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women
Health and safety at work: 8 August to become European day of remembrance for victims of accidents at work
docuLanguageListResources.leadText: The European Commission, European Parliament and Council signed today a joint declaration establishing a European day of remembrance for victims of accidents at work.

docuLanguageListResources.title: Remarks by Executive Vice-President Mînzatu and Commissioner Dombrovskis on the 2027 European Semester Autumn package
Commission calls for joint EU efforts to reduce tax gaps and boost public finances
docuLanguageListResources.leadText: Today, the European Commission published its Mind the Gap 2026 Communication, showing how enhanced tax compliance, improved governance of tax expenditures, better tax collection and more effective tax administration can help Member States protect public finances and create room for the investments Europe urgently needs.

docuLanguageListResources.title: Commission sets out key EU policy priorities for 2027 in its European Semester Autumn Package
docuLanguageListResources.leadText: The European Commission today adopted the 2027 European Semester Autumn Package, setting out economic, social and employment policy priorities.

docuLanguageListResources.title: Questions and answers on the 2027 European Semester Autumn Package
Commission imposes provisional import quotas on hybrid passenger vehicles
docuLanguageListResources.leadText: The European Commission today published provisional safeguard measures setting import quotas for certain hybrid vehicles. These restrictions are needed to protect EU industry against a sharp recent increase in imports of such vehicles. The measures will enter into force on 1 December and follow an investigation that showed imports of hybrid vehicles into the EU have increased significantly since 2023.

docuLanguageListResources.title: Statement by President von der Leyen on the 22nd package of sanctions against Russia
docuLanguageListResources.leadText: Today, we present our 22nd package of sanctions. The aim is to keep pressure on Russia to end their war of aggression in Ukraine. And we will continue to propose new sanctions until Russia shows genuine intent for a lasting peace in Ukraine. With this package, we are increasing the pressure in three ways.

docuLanguageListResources.title: Commission adopts guidelines implementing the visa ban on combatants in Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine
docuLanguageListResources.leadText: Today, alongside the proposal for the EU's 22nd sanctions package, the Commission is taking action to strengthen Europe's security, ensuring that those linked to Russia's war of aggression are banned from our territory and cannot become a security risk or the Union and its citizens.

docuLanguageListResources.title: Commission opens formal investigation into possible anticompetitive conduct by Coca-Cola Europacific Partners in the non-alcoholic drinks sector *
docuLanguageListResources.leadText: The European Commission has opened a formal antitrust investigation to assess whether Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (‘CCEP') has breached EU competition rules by (i) hindering the cross-border trade of carbonated soft drinks and sports drinks; and (ii) denying certain wholesale customers the possibility to negotiate the procurement of these products on a multi-country basis.

docuLanguageListResources.title: EU stood firm for ambition and implementation at COP31
docuLanguageListResources.leadText: Yesterday at the COP31 UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya, the European Union and all 27 Member States in unity showed the world their firm stance to limit global warming through the Paris Agreement and their determination to implement climate commitments already made among global partners.

docuLanguageListResources.title: Commission approves €1 billion Slovenian State aid to support closure of Premogovnik Velenje coal mine
docuLanguageListResources.leadText: The European Commission has approved, under EU State aid rules, a €1 billion Slovenian measure to cover exceptional costs related to the closure of the Premogovnik Velenje coal mine.

docuLanguageListResources.title: Commission welcomes European Citizens' Panel recommendations on Democratic Resilience
docuLanguageListResources.leadText: The European Citizens' Panel on Democratic Resilience concluded yesterday with its third and final session.

EU and Indonesia sign ambitious trade and investment agreements
docuLanguageListResources.leadText: The European Union and Indonesia today signed their Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), and Investment Protection Agreement (IPA).

docuLanguageListResources.leadText: Today, the European Commission partially greenlighted Malta's fifth and final payment request for €61.7 million under the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF), the centrepiece of NextGenerationEU.

Commission disburses €7.9 billion to strengthen Ukraine's financial stability and advance reform efforts
docuLanguageListResources.leadText: Today, the European Commission has released €7.9 billion to Ukraine to support financing needs and maintain the functioning of the country's public administration, as it continues to defend itself against Russia's war of aggression. This is the largest single disbursement to Ukraine made by the EU under the Ukraine Facility.

docuLanguageListResources.leadText: Today, the European Commission greenlighted the Netherlands' fifth and last payment request worth €1.7 billion under the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF), the centrepiece of NextGenerationEU.

docuLanguageListResources.title: EU and Jordan advance strategic partnership backed by €3 billion to boost investment, create jobs and strengthen regional stability
docuLanguageListResources.leadText: Today, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and Commissioner for the Mediterranean Dubravka Šuica took part in the EU-Jordan Investment Conference at the Dead Sea. Alongside His Majesty King Abdullah II bin Al-Hussein, President von der Leyen witnessed the signing of agreements to support Jordan's economic modernisation and resilience.

Almost €24 billion mobilised and 614 projects awarded for their support to critical technologies in Europe, according to Commission report
docuLanguageListResources.leadText: Today, the European Commission published the second annual report of the Strategic Technologies for Europe Platform (STEP), covering 2025.

docuLanguageListResources.title: Commission decides to refer Greece to the Court of Justice of the European Union for the non-implementation of individual aircraft identification in the field of civil aviation
docuLanguageListResources.leadText: Today, the European Commission decided to refer Greece (INFR(2024)2237) to the Court of Justice of the European Union for failing to implement the required aircraft identification technology, as mandated by Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/373, which governs air traffic management and navigation services.

docuLanguageListResources.title: Commission decides to refer Poland to the Court of Justice of the European Union for failing to align its rules with the Seveso III Directive
docuLanguageListResources.leadText: Today, the European Commission decided to refer Poland (INFR(2021)2067) to the Court of Justice of the European Union for failing to align its rules with the Seveso III Directive (Directive 2012/18/EU).

docuLanguageListResources.title: Commission decides to refer Austria to the Court of Justice of the European Union for incorrectly applying the European arrest warrant
docuLanguageListResources.leadText: Today, the European Commission decided to refer Austria (INFR(2020)2307) to the Court of Justice of the European Union for failing to comply with the Framework Decision on the European Arrest Warrant (2002/584/JHA).

Commission sets up new EU Sanctions Office and appoints new EU Sanctions Envoy
docuLanguageListResources.leadText: Today, the Commission has created the EU Sanctions Office to bring together the Commission's expertise on the entire sanctions lifecycle, from policy design to implementation, enforcement, and anti-circumvention, including outreach to and engagement with third countries.

docuLanguageListResources.title: Commission opens Erasmus+ 2027 call with over €5.3 billion for wider opportunities in education, training, youth and sport
docuLanguageListResources.leadText: Today, the European Commission opens the 2027 Erasmus+ call for proposals with a budget of over €5.3 billion. The call is expected to offer learning mobility experiences in all education sectors for an estimated 1.6 million participants and support over 120,000 organisations.
